svg.title: The fall in UK sulphur dioxide emissions
svg.desc: UK sulphur dioxide emissions fell from 6,518 thousand tonnes in 1970 to 84 thousand tonnes in 2024, about 99%, through less coal, low-sulphur fuels, scrubbers and international treaties from 1979.
svg.text: Acid rain: the problem we fixed
UK sulphur dioxide emissions, thousand tonnes. NAEI (1970) and Defra (2024).
About a 99% fall (my arithmetic across two inventory editions; Defra reports 98% since 1990).
How: less coal, low-sulphur fuels, scrubbers on power stations, and international treaties from 1979.
